bearing.guide.shaft.header: Shafts: Carrying Rotation in a Line
bearing.guide.shaft.text_1: A Shaft passes rotation on along its own axis, block after block, in a straight line
bearing.guide.shaft_casing.text_1: Put Andesite or Brass Casing on a Shaft to hide it inside a solid block; it keeps turning as before
bearing.guide.cogwheel.text_1: Cogwheels that touch each other side by side pass the rotation from one to the next
bearing.guide.cogwheel.text_2: Because of this, the shafts on two meshing cogs always spin in opposite directions
bearing.guide.cog_speedup.text_1: A large and a small cogwheel on parallel axes mesh when placed diagonally next to each other
bearing.guide.cog_speedup.text_2: Driving the small cog from the large one gives the small cog twice the speed
bearing.guide.cog_speedup.text_3: Drive it the other way round, from small to large, and the speed is cut in half
bearing.guide.cogwheel_casing.text_1: Cogwheels and Large Cogwheels can be wrapped in Andesite or Brass Casing too
bearing.guide.cogwheel_casing.text_2: Anything you attach after encasing stays still: the casing keeps its shaft openings closed
bearing.guide.cogwheel_casing.text_3: Use a Wrench on a face of the casing to open or close the shaft connection there
bearing.guide.large_cogwheel.text_1: Two Large Cogwheels can mesh at a right angle to each other
bearing.guide.large_cogwheel.text_2: This lets you carry the same speed over onto a different axis of rotation
bearing.guide.belt_connector.text_1: Use a belt item on one shaft, then on a second: a belt is stretched between the two
bearing.guide.belt_connector.text_2: Picked the wrong shaft? Sneak and Right-Click to drop the current selection
bearing.guide.belt_connector.text_3: More shafts can be fitted into the belt anywhere along its length
bearing.guide.belt_connector.text_4: Every shaft on the same belt turns at exactly the same speed and in the same direction
bearing.guide.belt_connector.text_5: Take an added shaft back out by using a Wrench on it
bearing.guide.belt_connector.text_6: Dyes give belts a new colour; this is purely cosmetic
bearing.guide.belt_directions.text_1: A belt cannot be stretched between just any two shafts
bearing.guide.belt_directions.text_3: 2. Up or down a 45 degree slope
bearing.guide.belt_directions.text_5: 4. On its side, joining two upright shafts
bearing.guide.belt_directions.text_6: That is the full list. A single belt may be anywhere from 2 to 20 blocks long
bearing.guide.belt_transport.text_1: A running belt carries items, mobs and players along with it
bearing.guide.belt_transport.text_2: Items can be lifted off a belt by Right-Clicking it bare-handed
bearing.guide.belt_casing.text_1: Andesite or Brass Casing can be put around a belt to dress it up
bearing.guide.belt_casing.text_2: Use a Wrench on an encased section to take its casing off again
bearing.guide.gearbox.text_1: Turning a corner with Large Cogwheels takes up a lot of room
bearing.guide.gearbox.text_2: A Gearbox does the same job in a single block
bearing.guide.gearbox.text_3: Shafts taken off to the sides turn as mirror images of each other
bearing.guide.gearbox.text_4: A shaft straight across from the input turns the opposite way
bearing.guide.clutch.text_1: Unpowered, a Clutch simply passes rotation straight through like a shaft
bearing.guide.clutch.text_2: A redstone signal disengages it: everything past the Clutch comes to a stop
bearing.guide.gearshift.text_1: Without a redstone signal, a Gearshift relays rotation straight through
bearing.guide.gearshift.text_2: A redstone signal flips it: the output side now spins the other way
bearing.guide.sequenced_gearshift.text_1: This gearbox runs a program: a series of steps, each lasting a set time
bearing.guide.sequenced_gearshift.text_2: Right-Click it to open the screen where the steps are set up
bearing.guide.sequenced_gearshift.text_3: A redstone pulse starts the sequence from the top
bearing.guide.sequenced_gearshift.text_4: When the last step is done it stops and waits for the next signal to run again
bearing.guide.sequenced_gearshift.text_5: A Redstone Comparator behind it outputs how far the sequence has got
bearing.guide.creative_motor.text_1: From a single block, the Creative Motor puts out rotation at any speed you choose
bearing.guide.creative_motor.text_2: Scroll over the value panel on its side to choose the speed it produces
bearing.guide.creative_motor_mojang.head: A Mojang Mystery
bearing.guide.water_wheel.text_1: A Water Wheel takes its power from flowing water running past it
bearing.guide.water_wheel.text_2: Adding water on more sides of the wheel will not make it any stronger
bearing.guide.water_wheel.text_3: Right-click the wheel with planks to swap the wood it is built from
bearing.guide.large_water_wheel.header: Power from a Large Water Wheel
bearing.guide.large_water_wheel.text_1: Large Water Wheels are also driven by flowing water next to them
bearing.guide.large_water_wheel.text_2: Putting water against further sides gains nothing extra
bearing.guide.large_water_wheel.text_3: Compared to the small wheel, they turn only half as fast...
bearing.guide.large_water_wheel.text_4: ...but in exchange they can carry far more stress
bearing.guide.large_water_wheel.text_5: Planks applied to it swap its wood type in the same way
bearing.guide.hand_crank.text_1: A Hand Crank is rotation powered by your own arm
bearing.guide.hand_crank.text_2: Counter-Clockwise turning lasts as long as Right-Click is held
bearing.guide.hand_crank.text_3: Do the same while Sneaking and it turns Clockwise
bearing.guide.valve_handle.header: Exact Turns with a Valve Handle
bearing.guide.valve_handle.text_1: A Valve Handle turns whatever it drives by an exact angle
bearing.guide.valve_handle.text_2: Set that angle by scrolling on its value panel
bearing.guide.valve_handle.text_3: Right-Click it once to perform a single turn
bearing.guide.valve_handle.text_4: Sneak and Right-Click to turn it back the other way
bearing.guide.valve_handle.text_5: Remember to set the Bearing so that it does not disassemble when it stops
bearing.guide.valve_handle.text_6: Dye a Valve Handle to change its colour
bearing.guide.chain_drive.text_1: A row of Chain Drives shares one rotation down the line
bearing.guide.chain_drive.text_2: Unlike cogwheels, every shaft along the chain turns in the same direction
bearing.guide.chain_drive.text_3: Any drive in the row may be turned 90 degrees to point its shaft another way
bearing.guide.chain_gearshift.text_1: Without power, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift works just like a normal Chain Drive
bearing.guide.chain_gearshift.text_2: Powered, it doubles the speed it hands on to the other drives in the row
bearing.guide.chain_gearshift.text_3: If the powered Gearshift is not where the rotation comes in, it halves its own speed instead
bearing.guide.chain_gearshift.text_4: Either way, the plain Chain Drives always turn twice as fast as the powered Gearshift
bearing.guide.chain_gearshift.text_5: An analog redstone signal lets you pick any ratio between 1 and 2
Setting Speed with a Speed Controller
A Rotation Speed Controller takes the rotation running through it and drives the Large Cogwheel on top
Scroll over the value panel on its side to set the speed it hands on
bearing.guide.speedometer.text_1: A Speedometer shows how fast the components it is attached to are turning
bearing.guide.speedometer.text_2: Engineer's Goggles show the exact figures when you look at the gauge
bearing.guide.speedometer.text_3: A Redstone Comparator reading the gauge gives off a signal that grows with the measured speed
bearing.guide.stressometer.text_1: A Stressometer shows how much of the network's Stress Capacity is in use
bearing.guide.stressometer.text_2: Engineer's Goggles show the exact figures when you look at the gauge
bearing.guide.stressometer.text_3: A Redstone Comparator reading the gauge gives off a signal that grows with the measured stress
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_1: The engine block goes against the wall of a Fluid Tank
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_2: Use a Shaft on the engine to give it a kinetic output
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_3: Supply the boiler with heat, water and size...
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_5: The smallest working boiler is made of 4 Fluid Tanks
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_6: Fuelled Blaze Burners underneath raise the power the boiler can deliver
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_7: Climbing a level needs a bigger boiler, more water and more heat
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_8: Look at the boiler while wearing Engineer's Goggles to see its current power level
bearing.guide.steam_engine.text_9: For every power level the boiler has, one more engine can run at full strength
bearing.guide.steam_whistle.text_1: A Steam Whistle goes on the side of a Fluid Tank
bearing.guide.steam_whistle.text_2: Once the tank is being heated enough...
bearing.guide.steam_whistle.text_3: ...it sounds a note whenever it receives a redstone signal
bearing.guide.steam_whistle.text_4: Using another Whistle on it makes it longer and drops its pitch
bearing.guide.steam_whistle.text_5: Use a Wrench on it to step through three octaves
bearing.guide.steam_whistle.text_6: Engineer's Goggles tell you which note a Whistle is currently set to
